_comment: The machine-readable export boundary: every path downstream projects consume, grouped by HOW it reaches them (which determines how changes propagate). Validated by .github/scripts/check-exports.js in qa.yml: every path must exist, and every raw-URL self-reference in the tree must point inside one of these paths. Anything not listed here is internal to this repo and safe to move.

inherited-rules.mode: fetched live by raw URL at session start — changes propagate immediately

installed-tooling.mode: installed via the plugin marketplace / SessionStart hook — propagates to the next session for projects carrying .claude/hooks/session-start.sh, otherwise on the env cache rebuild (~weekly); versioned by git SHA

copied-scaffolding.mode: copied into projects at bootstrap — snapshots that drift by design; /refresh-repo detects drift

referenced-docs.mode: read on demand via links — no copy, no install

domains._comment: The LOGICAL view, orthogonal to categories (which encode propagation): domain → compartment → paths. A compartment is the swappable unit — replace its file set honoring its interface and nothing outside it moves. Rendered visually at docs/site/logical-map.html; boundaries and swap procedure in MAINTAIN-REPO-USER-INSTRUCTIONS.md → Domain Boundaries. Validated by check-exports.js: every path must exist.

swap._comment: Swap classes over the domain view. PERMANENT paths evolve via PR and are never wholesale-replaced — this covers directives/ and the exported standards under docs/standards/, since both carry blocking criteria; the meta domain is permanent in its entirety, so every meta path is enumerated here too. ORCHESTRATORS are permanent AND define the flow/interfaces their components must fit — a new component does not exist until its orchestrator sequences it. Everything else is swappable within its compartment's interface.

classes._comment: Durability classes over the exported set — WHAT KIND of thing each file is, and therefore what happens to it as models improve. Independent of `swap` (which says whether a path may be replaced) and of `domains` (which says what it belongs to). Every path in `domains` must appear in exactly one class; check-exports.js enforces the partition, so this view cannot rot the way an unchecked diagram would. Drawn at docs/site/logical-map.html, which build-logical-map.js generates from this file.

standard.label: Standards
standard.blurb: State blocking criteria a change must satisfy. Model-independent: a smarter model still has to meet them.

orchestrator.label: Orchestrators
orchestrator.blurb: Define the flow and the interfaces components must fit. A component does not exist until its orchestrator sequences it.

behavioral.label: Behavioral scaffolding
behavioral.blurb: Tells a model HOW to act. The only class that decays as models improve — audit it whenever the model tier changes.

mechanical.label: Mechanical enforcement
mechanical.blurb: Runs with no model in the loop. Immune to model change; the backstop when scaffolding is trimmed.

artifact.label: Artifacts
artifact.blurb: Fill-in templates and scaffolds. Consumed by a project, never executed here.

reference.label: Reference
reference.blurb: Read on demand. Explains and illustrates; binds nothing on its own.

externals._comment: Vendor-owned capabilities this system depends on but does not contain — we hold only the sockets. To swap a vendor: rewire the listed socket files, never fork the vendor's code. serves = domain.compartment from the domains view. sockets = the files here that name/enable/configure it (must exist; validated).

considered._comment: Native capabilities evaluated by the upkeep mandate (CLAUDE.md -> Purpose) and NOT adopted wholesale. externals records what we depend on; this records what we looked at and declined, so an audit reads the verdict instead of re-deriving it. verdict: borrowed (an idea taken, the implementation stays) | rejected (does not fit) | deferred (fits, not yet done). stays = the path that keeps the job; must exist (validated).

commit-commands.rationale: Creates commits/PRs; /commit-chk verifies BEFORE a push. Complementary, not overlapping.

feature-dev.rationale: Generic explore/architect/review flow; /sdd-loop is bound to the imported directives as its constitution.

claude-md-management.rationale: Its claude-md-improver skill grades CLAUDE.md A-F; that rubric is copied into /audit-repo, so nothing loads the skill at runtime. Recorded under the PLUGIN name, which is what a marketplace manifest advertises and therefore what the parity diff sees.

hookify.rationale: Its hooks add dirname(CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT) to sys.path then `import hookify`, which assumes the plugin root's basename is the package. The versioned install layout (hookify/0.1.0/) puts a version dir there instead, so all four registered hooks -- PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, UserPromptSubmit -- fail with "No module named 'hookify'" on EVERY tool call. Not forkable (externals rule: rewire sockets, never fork vendor code). Revisit only if upstream stops assuming that layout; plugin-dev's hook-development skill covers the same authoring ground without hooks of its own.

skill-creator.rationale: Its eval MODEL (query + should-fire, scored over repeated runs) shaped the first local runner, which `claude plugin eval` has now replaced entirely. Its own runner is unusable: scripts/run_eval.py returns on the FIRST tool use of the FIRST assistant message, so any preamble reads as no-trigger -- it scored the known-good pdf skill 0.00. Nothing of it remains in the repo; kept as a rejected-with-reason so no audit re-adopts it for trigger testing.

update-config.rationale: Built-in skill for settings.json editing: permissions, env vars, and hook registration. Overlaps /refresh-repo Phase 1.5, which hand-writes jq to merge the SessionStart row and the permissions.allow block. Deferred rather than borrowed because refresh-repo's job is a NEGOTIATED sync (diff the installed copy against upstream, disposition each drift), not a settings edit; update-config performs the write but decides nothing. Revisit if refresh-repo's jq needs another repair - the write half should delegate then.

fewer-permission-prompts.rationale: Built-in skill that mines transcripts for common tool calls and proposes an allowlist. Our allowlist is not discovered from usage - it is an owner ruling (global.md -> Scheduling Tools Never Prompt) naming exactly six tools with recorded accepted residuals, deliberately excluding the riskier remote tools a usage-mined list would surface. Adopting it would widen the grant by exactly the mechanism the ruling rejects.

init.rationale: Built-in skill that writes a CLAUDE.md by reading the codebase. /new-repo writes one from templates/CLAUDE-template.md, which carries the imported directive URLs, the UI-test config table, the project-specific test scenarios table the ui-tester refuses to run without, and the reporting contract. A codebase-derived CLAUDE.md has none of those, and a new repo has no codebase to derive from.

claude-code-setup.rationale: Sets up Claude Code in an existing repo. /new-repo bootstraps against THIS fleet's standard: the workflow set, the composite actions, the Playwright kit, styles/, the marketplace + plugin enablement, and the SessionStart hook. Generic setup delivers none of it.

session-report.rationale: Summarises a session. /handoff-session is deliberately the opposite: global.md -> Handoffs Carry Only What Dies With the Session makes it delta-only, and a comprehensive summary is precisely the failure mode that ruling exists to prevent.

code-simplifier.rationale: Anthropic plugin, plus the built-in /simplify skill. Used for per-file quality cleanup; /audit-repo keeps only what neither does - repo-wide directive drift, the CLAUDE.md grade, native-parity, and structural soundness across the tree.

artifact-design.rationale: Built-in skill; the design-side sibling of artifact-diagramming and dataviz, both already borrowed. Authority for any published Artifact's design pass. design.md defers to it the way it defers to the other two.

artifact-capabilities.rationale: Built-in skill defining the runtime capabilities a published Artifact may declare. Required reading before /doc-comp publishes its diff as an Artifact rather than writing an undeliverable local file.

lsp-plugins.rationale: The twelve Anthropic language-server plugins (typescript-lsp, pyright-lsp, gopls-lsp, ...). This repo is markdown, small Node scripts and YAML; a language server buys nothing over node --check and the existing validators. Recorded as one entry so a future parity pass does not re-derive eleven verdicts.

output-styles.rationale: explanatory-output-style and learning-output-style change how a session narrates. global.md -> Plain Language First and Say It in Verbs already own that, as owner rulings; a plugin that overrides them would contradict the directives.

claude-security.rationale: Deep vulnerability scan that also generates and applies verified patches, with hooks of its own. The security job is already delegated to Anthropic natives recorded in externals (security-guidance plugin + built-in /security-review), and the toolkit maintains no security reviewer for it to replace. A heavier scan-and-patch tier suits a project with application code; install it per project, not fleet-wide from here.

ralph-loop.rationale: A Stop hook blocks session exit and re-feeds the SAME prompt until the model emits a completion-promise string. /sdd-loop iterates over spec -> plan -> tasks artifacts with the imported directives as the constitution, so completion is decided by the directives' gates (tests, CI, review), not by a string the model chooses to print.

ralph-wiggum.rationale: The same plugin as ralph-loop, advertised under its older name by the claude-code-plugins marketplace. Same verdict and reason; recorded separately because the parity diff matches manifest names.

simplify.rationale: Built-in skill; already covered by the code-simplifier entry, recorded under its own name because the parity diff matches names. /audit-repo recommends it as a follow-up and never runs it itself, since it APPLIES fixes and audit-repo is findings-only.

loop.rationale: Built-in skill that re-runs a prompt on an interval. git.md -> GitHub API Quota Economy says never poll for CI, deploy, or PR status (webhook wakes + ci-notify instead), and CLAUDE.md -> Notifications forbids arming a timed check-in as a substitute for a subscription. A recurring prompt is the mechanism both rulings exclude.

run.rationale: Built-in skill that launches and drives the app for a one-off look at a change. The ui-tester agent does a different job: it runs the project's Playwright suite against the URL CLAUDE.md names and writes the report the orchestrator reads, which is the evidence test.md asks for. Complementary, not overlapping.

anthropic-skills.rationale: Parent of the docx, pdf, pptx and xlsx file skills (plus browser, research and docs skills with no toolkit counterpart). The docx redline output is not wanted, because doc-comp's deliverable is a published Artifact, not a tracked-changes .docx. What still fits is INPUT: doc-comp does not say how to read a .docx or .pdf, and could hand that extraction to these skills where the session provides them. Not done yet.

project-artifact.rationale: Publishes a living project status page as a claude.ai artifact. This repo's published view is the logical map, generated from EXPORTS.json and checked in CI (build-logical-map.js --check) on GitHub Pages; a status page built from gathered state would be a second, unchecked view of the same repo.

playground.rationale: Generates single-file interactive HTML explorers. The logical map is the only interactive page here, and its behaviour is hand-written and held by the Repo Map UI Playwright suite; a generated explorer would carry none of those invariants.

out-of-domain.rationale: Plugins agent-sdk-dev, claude-opus-4-5-migration, code-modernization, cwc-makers, math-olympiad, mcp-apps, mcp-server-dev, mcp-tunnels and receipts, and built-in skills claude-api, workflow-authoring and keybindings-help. Each serves a job this repo and its toolkit do not have (SDK or MCP development, model migration, legacy modernisation, hardware onboarding, competition math, usage reports, API reference, Workflow scripts, keybindings). Recorded as one entry so a future parity pass does not re-derive twelve verdicts.
